fixes.explanation: No priest anywhere in this verse, baker. It says, "A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD." That's like me yelling at the oven after I forgot to set the timer. The verse puts the trouble on his own folly, and still his heart rages against the LORD.

Nope, this one's true, baker. Verse 4 says, "Wealth attracts many friends…" Solomon is describing how things go, and I think it's a little sad. The second half of the verse says a poor man is deserted by his friend.

Yes, baker. Verse 6 says, "Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver." Everybody wants to be close to the one handing things out. I think Solomon is noticing who people gather around.

The hard worker isn't in this verse, baker. Verse 6 says, "Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver." It's the gift giver who has everybody around him. Solomon is describing how people crowd toward whoever is handing things out.

Yes, baker. The verse says the one who safeguards understanding "…will find success." Safeguarding means guarding it like a fresh tray of cookies at a party. And the first half of verse 8 says the one who acquires wisdom loves himself.

The king isn't in this verse, baker. Verse 14 says, "Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD." Fathers hand down houses and wealth, but the verse says a prudent wife is from the LORD. I'd say that makes her worth more than any house.

Elders aren't in this verse, baker. Verse 14 says, "Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD." Fathers hand down houses and wealth, and the verse gives the LORD as the source of a prudent wife. I think that's a lovely thing to be told.

The king isn't in this verse, baker. Verse 17 says, "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender." A loan is something you expect to see again, and the verse says the LORD will repay. So the loan is made to the LORD, not the king.

Seeds and fields make a nice picture, but they aren't in this verse. Verse 17 says, "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender." The word Solomon uses is loan. And the LORD is the one on the receiving end.

True, baker. Verse 17 says, "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender." Think about that for a second. The one who showed kindness to the poor is the lender, and the LORD is the one who will repay.

This one's true, baker. Verse 17 says, "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender." The one who was kind to the poor is the lender, and the verse says the LORD will repay. So "False" sells the verse short.

That's right, baker. Verse 19 says, "A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again." Rescuing him once isn't the end of it. The verse says you will have to do so again.

The verse doesn't say anything about being alone, baker. It says, "A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again." The word is again. A second rescue is what the verse says is coming.

Secrets aren't part of this verse, baker. It says, "A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again." The word is again. Nothing in the verse is about doing it quietly.

Strangers don't come up in this verse, baker. It says, "The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar." Solomon sets being poor right next to being a liar. Poor wins that matchup, and the word that fits is liar.

This one is true, baker. Verse 23 says, "The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm." The verse ties the fear of the LORD to life and to resting content. That's the connection Solomon makes, so "False" doesn't fit.

Not quite, baker. Verse 24 says, "The slacker buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth." The verse doesn't have him eating every last bit. It says he will not bring his hand back to his mouth. Solomon is making laziness look ridiculous.

Sharing would be kind, but the verse doesn't show him doing it. Verse 24 says, "The slacker buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth." That's what the slacker does. Nobody else is mentioned in this verse.

That's a different reaction from the one in the verse, baker. Verse 25 says, "Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; rebuke the discerning man, and he will gain knowledge." The verse doesn't say the discerning man mocks anyone. It says he will gain knowledge.

That would be the opposite, baker. Verse 27 says, "If you cease to hear instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge." Learning is what happens when you hear instruction. The verse says if you cease to hear it, you will stray.
